why: These exports connect the two private service modules. The package entry exports only public service tags and app extensions, not middleware or rule internals.

state.name: clock

why: ADR 0099 and the user require a resource-owned plain clock. Its waits and clock mode are live resource state; service business state remains in data cells.

state.name: middleware

why: The rule operation checks the combined stop and call signal after its wait. The log skips writes after stop. Middleware must finish an accepted stopped reply before the owned listener closes.

state.name: listener

why: Only main owns the process signal. Core owns the listener resource and invokes its close; the real entry and stopped-call HTTP tests prove closure.

state.name: listener

why: After listening, the resource registers its owned close before returning. Core cleans up an aborted build; adding another scope or signal shutdown path would duplicate Core ownership.

state.name: finishDelivery

why: The caller deliver checks its combined signal before this operation. The send operation passes that signal to fetch. After send is awaited this operation makes no further writes.

state.name: webhooks

why: Core owns the subscription resource. Its deliver operation uses the service stop signal and call signal; close removes the subscription through defer.

state.name: inFlight

why: ADR 0100 puts live pending promises in a resource. Only settled replies are plain data. The pipelined HTTP proof checks sharing while a key is pending.

state.name: inFlight

why: The resource owns pending key promises and clears them on Core close. No IO loop runs here; Hono completes accepted replies before listener close.

state.name: pay

why: Expected Duffel refusals are promised HTTP replies, not failed Core operations. The handler returns the named code and status to its caller.

state.name: intentKey

why: Pending key promises belong to the inFlight resource. Hono runs the one synchronous business operation between key reservation and reply retention; no timer or IO loop runs inside key storage. The real pipelined HTTP test proves pending sharing and completion.
